hypothesis: A peer sends a WRITE_MULTIPLE_COILS request whose quantity 'nb' and byte count 'nb_bits' disagree. The only consistency check is 'nb_bits * 8 < nb'. modbus_set_bits_from_bytes then reads ceil(nb/8) bytes from &req[offset+6]. If any backend delivers fewer data bytes than the declared byte count, or the MODBUS_MAX_WRITE_BITS limit from the header lets ceil(nb/8) data bytes extend past the received frame, the read goes beyond the received bytes or the request buffer.
evidence_source: Line 945 accepts the request when nb_bits*8 >= nb, with nb up to MODBUS_MAX_WRITE_BITS. Line 969 calls modbus_set_bits_from_bytes(tab_bits, mapping_address, nb, &req[offset + 6]), which reads (nb+7)/8 bytes. The receive path reads exactly req[offset+5] data bytes (compute_data_length_after_meta, line 314).
